records.title: Decompression Illness Treated with the Hart-Kindwall Protocol in a Monoplace Chamber
records.locator: Case Report and Discussion, PDF pp. 2–4
records.note: The authors clinically diagnosed severe altitude DCI during actual aircraft operation and discuss pulmonary barotrauma with micro-AGE as a possible explanation. The exposure and later monoplace treatment took place in different settings.

pressure_history.post_decompression_pure_oxygen: reported, time and flow not specified

observations.outcome_window: Symptoms documented on descent and immediately after landing. Emergency treatment roughly four hours after decompression, two follow-up treatment days, and return to flight duty at two weeks.
observations.locator: Case Report and Discussion, PDF pp. 2–4
observations.note: Clinical DCI diagnosis. Authors considered pulmonary barotrauma with micro-arterial gas embolism. No definite DCS subtype or eligible flight denominator. The 2023 translation describes the same episode.

records.title: 第1種装置を用いてHart-Kindwall治療表により加療した減圧障害の1例
records.locator: Printed p. 48, second-publication footnote and case presentation pp. 45–46
records.note: The footnote explicitly identifies the English article e935534 as the original. The indexed publisher text was accessible. Direct PDF download returned HTTP 404. The translation describes the same patient and adds no count. The Japanese Discussion says three minutes or less above 18,000 ft, while the English original specifies less than three minutes. Prefer the original's stated bound and retain the translation's wording.
